questions.answer: To find \(f_x\), treat \(y\) as a constant and differentiate with respect to \(x\). We have \(\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x^3)=3x^2\), \(\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(2xy)=2y\), and \(\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(y^2)=0\). Therefore \(f_x=3x^2+2y\).
To find \(f_y\), treat \(x\) as a constant and differentiate with respect to \(y\). The term \(x^3\) becomes \(0\), \(2xy\) becomes \(2x\), and \(y^2\) becomes \(2y\). Hence \(f_y=2x+2y\).
When differentiating with respect to \(x\), \(y\) is constant. Use the chain rule with inner function \(xy\), whose \(x\)-derivative is \(y\). Thus \(f_x=e^{xy}\cdot y\). Therefore \(f_x=ye^{xy}\).
Treat \(x\) as a constant and apply the chain rule. The derivative of \(\sin(xy)\) is \(\cos(xy)\) times the \(y\)-derivative of \(xy\), which is \(x\). Therefore \(f_y=x\cos(xy)\).
First differentiate with respect to \(x\): \(f_x=4x^3y+3y^2\), treating \(y\) as constant. Differentiate \(f_x\) again with respect to \(x\): \(f_{xx}=12x^2y+0\). Therefore \(f_{xx}=12x^2y\).

The notation \(f_{xy}\) means differentiate first with respect to \(x\), then with respect to \(y\). First \(f_x=2xy^3+5\). Now differentiate this with respect to \(y\): \(f_{xy}=2x\cdot 3y^2+0=6xy^2\).
First find the partial derivative with respect to \(x\), treating \(y\) as constant. We get \(f_x=2xy+0=2xy\). Substitute \((x,y)=(1,2)\): \(f_x(1,2)=2(1)(2)=4\). Therefore \(f_x(1,2)=4\).

questions.prompt: For \(f(x,y)=x^2+xy+y^2\), find the linear approximation to \(f\) at \((1,1)\).
questions.answer: The linear approximation is \(L(x,y)=f(a,b)+f_x(a,b)(x-a)+f_y(a,b)(y-b)\). Here \(f(1,1)=3\), \(f_x=2x+y\), so \(f_x(1,1)=3\), and \(f_y=x+2y\), so \(f_y(1,1)=3\). Therefore \(L(x,y)=3+3(x-1)+3(y-1)\).
Compute both mixed partials. First \(f_x=3x^2y^2\), so \(f_{xy}=6x^2y\). Next \(f_y=2x^3y\), so \(f_{yx}=6x^2y\). Since both expressions are equal, \(f_{xy}=f_{yx}=6x^2y\).

questions.prompt: For \(z=x^2y+y^3\), estimate the change in \(z\) near \((2,1)\) when \(dx=0.1\) and \(dy=-0.2\).
questions.answer: Use the differential \(dz\approx z_xdx+z_ydy\). We have \(z_x=2xy\) and \(z_y=x^2+3y^2\). At \((2,1)\), \(z_x=4\) and \(z_y=7\). Thus \(dz\approx 4(0.1)+7(-0.2)=0.4-1.4=-1.0\). The estimated change is \(-1\).
